_readme: Egyptian agricultural literature found for wheat, maize, faba bean and berseem. HOW THESE WERE READ: via web search, from abstracts / visible excerpts only, NOT full texts. Therefore every entry has verified_by_expert=false and must be checked by an agronomist before it is used to drive a recommendation. These are experimental results at named research stations, NOT official Ministry of Agriculture recommendations. 1 feddan = 0.42 ha = 4200 m2. Water numbers from different methods (applied irrigation experiments vs CROPWAT-modelled crop water use) are NOT comparable and are shown as ranges, never merged into one value.

planting_window.note: Water need rose with later sowing in R01 (CROPWAT-8).

water.what: CROPWAT-8 modelled requirement; lowest for sowing in the first week of November 2022, highest for the first week of January 2023
applied irrigation, three irrigation regimes at the 5 December sowing date (a different, experimental regime; cultivar Shandaweel 1, Upper Egypt)

wheat.comparability_warning: The two ranges differ by a factor of ~2-3 because they measure different things (modelled crop requirement vs deficit-irrigation treatments applied in a specific station/cultivar). No single 'wheat water requirement' is adopted.

planting_window.value: about mid-October to mid-November; yield fell when sowing was delayed beyond 1 November in the North Delta
planting_window.note: Late sowing reduced broomrape (Orobanche) infestation at Sakha (R08) but early sowing gave the highest yield for Misr 3: a real trade-off needing local advice.

water.value: 609.41 (rainfed after planting irrigation) to 1601.46 m3/feddan applied (4 irrigations excl. planting)
water.what: seasonal applied water incl. rainfall, Sakha
four irrigation treatments, Sakha; each extra cm of applied water added ~10.5 kg seed/feddan

faba_bean.other: 0.60 of the irrigation requirement gave the highest water-use efficiency under drip in the North Delta (R06, R07); this is an efficiency optimum, not a yield maximum.

planting_window.value: 1 to mid-October best; mid-September to end of October acceptable

water.what: clay soils, North Delta, cut-off irrigation trial
two sowing methods, Kafr El-Sheikh (3013.94 = average of the wet-sowing method)

planting_window.value: May (1-15 May gave the best results; later sowing reduced yield)
planting_window.note: Hot-summer sowing in July was worst for water-use efficiency (R14).

water.value: 6171 to 7321 m3/ha applied (= about 2592 to 3075 m3/feddan)

rotation_evidence.found: Only that SC10 maize was grown after Egyptian clover (R15) and after faba bean (R16) in these experiments. This shows the sequences are practised; it is NOT evidence of the size of any soil, nitrogen, water or income benefit.
rotation_evidence.gap: No Egyptian source quantifying benefits of wheat -> faba bean -> maize or wheat -> berseem -> maize was found in this pass. Wheat, faba bean and berseem are ALL winter crops (sown Oct-Nov), so the three-stage sequences cannot fit one calendar year: the 2-year cycle length used in the project is an analyst assumption that an agronomist must define.
